key_insight: A single deep model jointly learns to predict bioactivity and reconstruct molecules, and uses its learned representation to quantify distribution shift—enabling reliable discovery of active compounds at the edge of chemical space, validated by prospective kinase inhibitor hits.
problem_solved: Addresses unreliable bioactivity prediction when models encounter molecules outside their training distribution by providing a principled, model-internal measure of distribution shift and using it to guide prospective experimental discovery.
method: Train a multitask encoder–decoder model that simultaneously reconstructs molecular structure and predicts bioactivity from the same latent representation.
Derive a principled distribution-shift / out-of-distribution score from the learned representation (latent-space / likelihood-based), and use it to flag predictions with low trust.
Prospectively screen and experimentally validate predictions, discovering active inhibitors for two clinically relevant kinases to demonstrate real-world utility.
impact: Provides a practical framework for building safer, more trustworthy molecular ML models by coupling generative reconstruction with prediction and OOD scoring—improving hit discovery reliability in drug discovery pipelines.
visual_elements: Schematic of the joint model: encoder -> shared latent space -> decoder (reconstruction) and predictor (bioactivity)
2D chemical-space map (latent embedding) showing training distribution, test compounds, and OOD score heatmap
Bar/ROC plots comparing predictive accuracy and OOD detection performance, plus a trust-threshold illustration
Example structures of experimentally validated kinase inhibitors with measured activity bars
paper_title: Molecular deep learning at the edge of chemical space
paper_authors: Derek van Tilborg, Luke Rossen, Francesca Grisoni
